scope: Read-only source and existing-evidence audit; no training/source modifications or launches
conclusion: No missing official short/refusal/format safeguard was found in the active OpenRLHF PURE PRM-only path. For the same logits, groups, lengths, masks and log probabilities, official signal functions preserve the observed wrong positive updates. This is not a claim that the complete official recipe generates the same responses or frequencies.

findings.name: generation_minimum
findings.finding: min_tokens=1, special tokens retained. This prevents zero raw emitted tokens, not semantically empty or short irrelevant content.

findings.name: prompt
findings.finding: Official default explicitly requests steps separated by double newline. Our archived prepared Question/Answer prompt omits that clause; actual content is preserved for A/B comparability.

findings.name: eos_processing
findings.finding: process_sequences sets a processed EOS endpoint even at generation cap; at least one action is kept. No refusal/semantic-empty check.

findings.name: step_boundary
findings.finding: Tokenizer IDs whose decoded strings end with double newline are separators; final processed EOS is also a scored step. A no-separator response has one scored step.

findings.name: prm_input
findings.finding: Retain actor prompt IDs; replace each step-ending separator or EOS with a single newline, score that newline position. No separate judge prompt or completion-quality filter.

findings.name: signed_softmin
findings.finding: Two-class logits become p_positive minus p_negative and softmin weights at temperature0.1. With exactly one step the softmin weight is exactly1; a wrongly high PRM score remains positive.

findings.name: baseline
findings.finding: Token baseline is total peer process reward divided by total actual peer action length, multiplied by content-token count of each current step. No correctness/refusal filtering.

findings.name: optional_verifier
findings.finding: Only reward_mode containing VR uses solved minus1 followed by sequence leave-one-out and adds it at the final boundary. In an all-wrong group this entire verifier advantage is zero.

findings.name: kl_return_boundary_mask
findings.finding: After baseline subtract fixed KL; reverse cumulative return; set separator and final boundary advantages0. Boundary masking does not remove positive credit from preceding content tokens.

findings.name: normalization
findings.finding: Once-normalize global rollout token advantages, preserve pre-existing zeros. Count excludes zeros while variance numerator retains them; source semantics preserved locally.

findings.name: normalization_call_site
findings.finding: Normalize once before PPO train unless explicitly disabled; replay buffer cleared afterward.

findings.name: ppo_safeguard
findings.finding: PPO ratio clip0.2 and avg_ratio>10 multiplies loss by0. Neither detects incorrect math/refusal; measured three rows have ratio1.

findings.name: reward_clip_argument
findings.finding: reward_clip_range defaults(-10,10), but PURE active experience path imports and never calls compute_reward; no active clamp found there. Such bounds would not change observed positive signed scores anyway.

findings.name: lora_default
findings.finding: lora_rank default0; official train_pure.sh does not enable LoRA, so its learning rate is a full-parameter recipe.

findings.name: official_recipe
findings.finding: Temperature0.5, PRMVR, group4, rollout64prompts, trainbatch128, LR5e-7, KL.001, prompt1024, generation2048, distributedZeRO2. These are not our pilot batch/LoRA/prompt settings.

findings.name: scheduler
findings.finding: Constant scheduler, zero warmup. CLI lr_warmup_ratio declaration is not used in this active scheduler.

findings.name: official_admitted_failure
findings.finding: Official documentation says irrelevant thanks/happy-birthday outputs can score positive, describes hacking and a step100 pre-hacking checkpoint; token baseline addresses excessively long single-step collapse, not all semantically empty responses.

differences: Eq7 uses fixed maximum length N instead of actual peer length in this older OpenRLHF branch
Paper temperature1, group8, rollout64prompts, minibatch512, generation8192,500steps for Qwen-Math
Paper LR1e-6 VR/hybrid and5e-7 PRM; our two arms share5e-7 for controlled pilot
Paper reports best checkpoint; our fixed shared-stage pilot does not select by test score
paper_version.mechanism: Paper explicitly describes meaningless/empty replies receiving high causal-PRM reward and uses auxiliary ground truth to mitigate it; min-form delays rather than eliminates this failure.

adaptation_limits: Official example is full-parameter finetuning; our actor is LoRA rank16 alpha32. Same numerical LR is not same effective policy update and is not a validated LoRA optimum.
Our shared single A100 execution uses32responses/update rather than distributed official256responses/rollout or final-paper512.
Our actor prompt and original repaired verifier are retained from prior project, not replaced by the official prompt and verifier.
Our actor/vLLM initialization uses TRL only as runtime and frozen reference disables adapters; rewards/baseline/normalization/loss are official extracted functions, not TRL GRPO.

Safe FP32 merged-copy to BF16 vLLM avoids frozen-base merge/unmerge drift but introduces numerical differences from unmerged-LoRA training. Step1 first-layer q/gate check found only0.028695/0.036817percent BF16 weight entries changed; this does not prove whole-model or later updates are ineffective.
Our LoRA pilot can test feasibility and early behavior under this adapted protocol; it cannot alone reproduce or refute full-paper performance.
not_claimed: Three pathological examples are not proof of trained collapse or measured downstream accuracy drop.
Positive mean advantage is a loss coefficient, not a gradient norm or proportion of total parameter update.
Normalization rescales these errors but did not create their positive sign.
Switching to PRMVR is a method/experimental-arm change, not a missing bug fix; no such change was made.
